left.prediction: Any protocol family that is pairwise equal in the induced calculus should admit a canonical cost-minimizing representative whose guard signature is unique up to symmetry, discoverable in at most one normalization pass.
left.measurement: enumerate equivalent protocols and compare their guard signatures after normalization.
left.intervention: apply a normalization pass that only rewrites preparation words, not probe/readout roles.
left.expected_observation: one canonical representative per equality class, with a unique guard signature modulo admitted symmetry.
left.novelty_reason: local protocol equality does not force a canonical cost-minimizing representative or uniqueness of guard signature.

left.prediction: If a boundary term appears before the probe in one history class, then every symmetry-equivalent class must either show the same boundary term or a strictly cheaper preparation that preserves the same terminal partition within five trials.
left.measurement: compare boundary timing across symmetry-equivalent history classes.
left.intervention: permute the history by admitted symmetry and repeat the same guarded protocol.
left.expected_observation: boundary timing is symmetry-stable unless replaced by a cheaper preparation with the same terminal partition.
left.novelty_reason: the left-side structure allows symmetry, but not the cost-stability tradeoff coupled to boundary timing.

left.prediction: A null-value collapse after a failed guard should predictably separate into two classes on the next admissible probe: recoverable nulls and permanent nulls, with the split visible after one continuation readout.
left.measurement: track post-failure readout classes after the next admissible probe.
left.intervention: force a guard failure, then resume with the nearest admissible continuation.
left.expected_observation: two distinct null classes, one recoverable and one permanent, rather than a single generic failure state.
left.novelty_reason: the local theory labels guard failure, but does not itself force a recoverable/permanent null dichotomy.

right.prediction: Among measurement protocols equal in induced partition, there exists a unique lowest-cost detector/preparation split after one calibration normalization, and any alternative split will differ by a typed boundary event.
right.measurement: compare equivalent protocols after calibration normalization and cost decomposition.
right.intervention: renormalize detector calibration while keeping the excitation class fixed.
right.expected_observation: a unique lowest-cost split, with all other equal partitions incurring a boundary event or extra cost.
right.novelty_reason: instrument theory does not by itself force uniqueness of the cost split among equal partitions.

right.prediction: If a symmetry-related mechanism pair is separated only after a weak overdrive, then every later repetition should preserve the same separator unless a lower-cost preparation is found within four runs.
right.measurement: repeat the separating protocol under the same symmetry class and varying weak overdrive.
right.intervention: slightly tune excitation amplitude while holding preparation admissibility fixed.
right.expected_observation: stable separator behavior across repeats, with only cost-reducing preparation changes able to alter it.
right.novelty_reason: the apparatus side permits symmetry, but not persistence of a separator tied to cost reductions.

right.prediction: Invalid-preparation aborts should split into two observable classes after one retry: hard invalidity and near-valid recoverability, and the class should be readable from the detector's pre-excitation status alone.
right.measurement: perform one retry just inside the admissibility boundary and compare abort class.
right.intervention: adjust the preparation to the nearest admissible setting, then repeat.
right.expected_observation: a binary abort taxonomy visible before excitation, rather than a generic invalid state.
right.novelty_reason: invalid preparation is allowed, but a pre-excitation hard-vs-near-valid split is not forced locally.

left_fingerprint.constraint_class: A learner has finite histories under a partial right action and a version space of compatible completions. Candidate experiments are guarded preparation words, one probe, and a continuation readout. Learned generators reduce preparation cost but cannot manufacture epistemic value. Select experiments that partition compatible completions while preserving typed boundaries and external outcome authority.
left_fingerprint.abstract_form: A protocol acts on a versioned response object. Its value is the outcome partition it induces per guarded execution cost; composition separates preparation, probe, and readout.

invariants.carrier: compatible partial response mechanisms over finite histories
invariants.protocol: guarded preparation then probe then continuation readout
invariants.equality: two protocols are equal when they induce the same outcome partition on compatible mechanisms
invariants.composition: preparations compose only while guards remain admitted; probe and readout retain distinct ownership
invariants.symmetry: histories or preparations related by admitted equivariance share predictions and cost coordinates
invariants.boundary: reset, degeneration, or regime change is a typed response rather than a discarded sample
invariants.cost: primitive execution, irreversibility, and readout cost are explicit and skills may reduce preparation cost only
invariants.authority: external observation decides the response and task status
invariants.failure: a flat partition kills epistemic value; guard failure falls back before the probe

left_fingerprint.home_field: interactive control, reinforcement learning, graph search, adaptive compilation

right_fingerprint.constraint_class: A spectroscopy apparatus has candidate mechanisms, reusable preparation procedures, controlled excitations, response readouts, symmetries, and destructive or regime-changing degenerations. Select measurements whose predicted responses separate mechanisms relative to preparation and measurement cost.
right_fingerprint.abstract_form: A protocol prepares a carrier, applies a controlled excitation, and reads a response whose partition distinguishes compatible mechanisms; degenerations remain typed responses.

invariants.carrier: candidate physical mechanisms compatible with prior measurements
invariants.protocol: preparation then controlled excitation then response measurement
invariants.equality: two measurements are equal when they induce the same response partition on candidate mechanisms
invariants.composition: preparation procedures compose under validity guards while excitation and detector retain distinct roles
invariants.symmetry: symmetry-related preparations and mechanisms transport response predictions
invariants.boundary: destruction, saturation, or phase change is a typed measured outcome
invariants.cost: sample preparation, excitation, detector, and destructive-measurement costs are explicit
invariants.authority: instrument calibration and observed response decide the measurement consequence
invariants.failure: a flat predicted spectrum has no discriminative value; invalid preparation aborts before excitation

left.prediction: Any protocol family that is pairwise equal in the induced calculus should admit a canonical cost-minimizing representative whose guard signature is unique up to symmetry, discoverable in at most one normalization pass.
left.measurement: enumerate equivalent protocols and compare their guard signatures after normalization.
left.intervention: apply a normalization pass that only rewrites preparation words, not probe/readout roles.
left.expected_observation: one canonical representative per equality class, with a unique guard signature modulo admitted symmetry.
left.novelty_reason: local protocol equality does not force a canonical cost-minimizing representative or uniqueness of guard signature.

left.prediction: If a boundary term appears before the probe in one history class, then every symmetry-equivalent class must either show the same boundary term or a strictly cheaper preparation that preserves the same terminal partition within five trials.
left.measurement: compare boundary timing across symmetry-equivalent history classes.
left.intervention: permute the history by admitted symmetry and repeat the same guarded protocol.
left.expected_observation: boundary timing is symmetry-stable unless replaced by a cheaper preparation with the same terminal partition.
left.novelty_reason: the left-side structure allows symmetry, but not the cost-stability tradeoff coupled to boundary timing.

left.prediction: A null-value collapse after a failed guard should predictably separate into two classes on the next admissible probe: recoverable nulls and permanent nulls, with the split visible after one continuation readout.
left.measurement: track post-failure readout classes after the next admissible probe.
left.intervention: force a guard failure, then resume with the nearest admissible continuation.
left.expected_observation: two distinct null classes, one recoverable and one permanent, rather than a single generic failure state.
left.novelty_reason: the local theory labels guard failure, but does not itself force a recoverable/permanent null dichotomy.

right.prediction: Among measurement protocols equal in induced partition, there exists a unique lowest-cost detector/preparation split after one calibration normalization, and any alternative split will differ by a typed boundary event.
right.measurement: compare equivalent protocols after calibration normalization and cost decomposition.
right.intervention: renormalize detector calibration while keeping the excitation class fixed.
right.expected_observation: a unique lowest-cost split, with all other equal partitions incurring a boundary event or extra cost.
right.novelty_reason: instrument theory does not by itself force uniqueness of the cost split among equal partitions.

right.prediction: If a symmetry-related mechanism pair is separated only after a weak overdrive, then every later repetition should preserve the same separator unless a lower-cost preparation is found within four runs.
right.measurement: repeat the separating protocol under the same symmetry class and varying weak overdrive.
right.intervention: slightly tune excitation amplitude while holding preparation admissibility fixed.
right.expected_observation: stable separator behavior across repeats, with only cost-reducing preparation changes able to alter it.
right.novelty_reason: the apparatus side permits symmetry, but not persistence of a separator tied to cost reductions.

right.prediction: Invalid-preparation aborts should split into two observable classes after one retry: hard invalidity and near-valid recoverability, and the class should be readable from the detector's pre-excitation status alone.
right.measurement: perform one retry just inside the admissibility boundary and compare abort class.
right.intervention: adjust the preparation to the nearest admissible setting, then repeat.
right.expected_observation: a binary abort taxonomy visible before excitation, rather than a generic invalid state.
right.novelty_reason: invalid preparation is allowed, but a pre-excitation hard-vs-near-valid split is not forced locally.

left_constraint_class: Boundary-conditioned skill acquisition over a composable partial action system. Prior authoritative completion evidence labels intervention-bearing edges; current task-open receipts refute reached candidates. A held-out-certified target may be a relation among source factors, operation, and attempted effect, while the runtime currently stores only unary state predicates.
right_constraint_class: Guarded-command and relational program semantics. A command denotes a relation between initial states, operations, and outcomes; a postcondition is transported backward through sequential composition by weakest precondition. Tests witness or refute contracts, while representation changes are valid only when relational behavior commutes.
mother_structure: Guarded relation lattice with backward transport

duplicates.mother_structure: Backward-transported contract bundle over a quotient presentation

left.carrier: A bundle of guarded partial morphisms indexed by observation charts
left.target: An evidence-owned contract on source-operation-effect morphisms
left.evidence: Boundary positives and task-open refutations act as section constraints on the same bundle
left.coordinate_change: Joint equivariance preserves the bundle while quotienting can erase operation identity
left.composition: Terminal-edge requirements pull back through guarded morphism composition
left.failure: A unary quotient forgets the bundle coordinate and aliases distinct intervention lines

right.carrier: A bundle of command relations indexed by representations
right.target: A relational contract with exact backward image under composition
right.evidence: Test passes and failures constrain sections of the bundle
right.coordinate_change: Simulation/conjugacy preserves the bundle across representations
right.composition: Weakest-precondition is the pullback operation on the bundle
right.failure: Unary summaries collapse the bundle and overidentify behaviors

left.prediction: When two observation charts are jointly equivariant, the same held-out target should admit a single transport rule even if one chart alone cannot express it.
left.measurement: Fit transport rules separately in each chart and jointly across charts; compare held-out error.
left.intervention: Train a joint model with a shared latent relation but distinct chart projections.
left.expected_observation: Joint training resolves a target family that remains ambiguous in either chart alone.
left.novelty_reason: This predicts a specific advantage of shared relational transport, not merely more data or a larger model.

left.prediction: A boundary edge with a given operation word will induce a backward constraint that predicts a source condition not recoverable from source factors alone.
left.measurement: Check whether the back-propagated constraint improves source-side prediction only when operation words are included.
left.intervention: Remove operation words from the input and compare against a model that retains them.
left.expected_observation: The operation-aware model recovers a source condition missed by the factor-only model.
left.novelty_reason: The prediction isolates transport as a necessary ingredient, which the left theory’s local vocabulary alone does not force.

right.prediction: A contract exact in one representation will remain exact after a semantics-preserving representation change, but only if the precondition is stored as a relational bundle section rather than a unary summary.
right.measurement: Compare exactness before and after reparameterization for both bundle-aware and unary encodings.
right.intervention: Encode the same contract in a relational section form and in a unary summary form, then apply a representation change.
right.expected_observation: Bundle-aware exactness survives; unary exactness degrades or becomes ambiguous.
right.novelty_reason: This is a sharpened representation-invariance test that local semantics alone does not require.

right.prediction: Two contracts that coincide on unary tests will separate when lifted to the relational bundle, producing different backward images for the same command sequence.
right.measurement: Run a search over contract pairs matched on unary summaries and compare their weakest preconditions.
right.intervention: Introduce a relational test harness that distinguishes outcome-sensitive sections.
right.expected_observation: At least one unary-collapsed pair splits after bundle lift.
right.novelty_reason: The bundle lift predicts a concrete alias-breaking witness rather than a generic expressivity increase.

left.refuter: No cross-chart family exhibits joint expressivity beyond the best single chart.
left.gate: If joint equivariant transport never outperforms the best single-chart fit on held-out targets, reject the correspondence on the left side.
left.receipt: Save the chart-specific and joint metrics, plus the held-out target list.

left.refuter: Operation words never change source prediction once factor features are fixed.
left.gate: If operation-aware and factor-only models are indistinguishable across the benchmark, the bundle claim fails on the left side.
left.receipt: Store the ablation results and the matched-feature comparison.

right.refuter: Unary summaries remain exact after every representation change in the benchmark.
right.gate: If unary summaries never lose exactness, reject the need for a relational bundle on the right side.
right.receipt: Record the contract encodings, representation maps, and exactness outcomes.

right.refuter: Relational bundle lifting never produces a new separation among unary-collapsed contract pairs.
right.gate: If no aliasing is broken by the lift, the shared mother structure is unsupported on the right side.
right.receipt: Archive the unary-matched pairs and the lifted backward-image computations.

left.target: An evidence-owned relation on (source, operation, effect) triples, with unary state predicates as a projection of the triple relation

left.failure: Unary state predicates are the quotient that forgets operation identity and collapses distinct task consequences

right.carrier: A command calculus whose elements are guarded state-transition relations
right.target: A postcondition relation over initial state, command, and outcome
right.evidence: Passing and failing executions label the relation but do not create authority
right.coordinate_change: Simulation or conjugacy acts as a relation-preserving reindexing of presentations
right.composition: Weakest-precondition transport backward through command composition
right.failure: Unary invariants are the quotient that forgets action dependence

left.prediction: There exists a minimal non-unary held-out target whose backward transport through one guarded operation word is not determined by the learned unary state predicate alone.
left.measurement: Compare prediction error of a unary-only classifier against a triple-relational classifier on a fixed held-out set of source-operation-effect queries.
left.intervention: Collapse the runtime representation to unary predicates, then re-expand by adding one operation-sensitive relational feature and re-evaluate held-out targets.
left.horizon: Within 3 evaluation rounds on the same benchmark split.
left.expected_observation: Unary-only accuracy plateaus while the relation-aware model recovers a previously misclassified family of boundary-conditioned targets.
left.novelty_reason: Local skill-acquisition theory may already motivate action sensitivity, but it does not force the existence of a specific held-out family that becomes separable only after adding one relational lift.

left.prediction: A chart change that preserves the underlying triple relation will preserve cross-chart success even when the individually canonicalized source and effect factors disagree.
left.measurement: Track agreement between charts on the same held-out targets before and after a joint reparameterization.
left.intervention: Apply a nontrivial observation-chart change that jointly mixes source and effect coordinates while keeping the relation fixed.
left.horizon: Across 1 chart transformation and 1 retraining pass.
left.expected_observation: Factorwise features change, but relation-level predictions remain stable for the same held-out targets.
left.novelty_reason: This separates preserved relational behavior from preserved marginals; the side theory alone does not require a chart-mixing invariance test.

left.prediction: A boundary-positive edge and a task-open refutation can coexist on different representatives of the same unary state, forcing a quotient failure visible as a contradiction after backward transport.
left.measurement: Count unary states that map to both positive and refuting edge labels under the same transport rule.
left.intervention: Force two representatives to share the same unary state encoding while keeping their operation words distinct.
left.expected_observation: At least one unary collision produces opposite transport outcomes for distinct operation words.
left.novelty_reason: The mother structure predicts an explicit quotient-collapse witness; neither local theory alone forces this exact collision pattern.

right.measurement: Compare exactness of inferred preconditions under unary vs relational contract languages on the same command suite.
right.intervention: Replace unary test assertions with relation-aware postconditions while keeping the command sequence fixed.
right.expected_observation: Unary contracts either overapproximate or underapproximate, while relational contracts recover an exact preimage for the same command composition.
right.novelty_reason: Program semantics already admits weakest preconditions, but this prediction isolates a specific lift gap that should appear only when action dependence matters.

right.prediction: A simulation or conjugacy that preserves behavior globally will still fail if tests are projected to unary state summaries, yielding a false mismatch that disappears under relational comparison.
right.measurement: Measure disagreement between unary-summary test results and relation-level equivalence checks under a representation change.
right.intervention: Apply a semantics-preserving reparameterization and evaluate both unary and relational test suites.
right.horizon: Across 1 representation change and 1 regression run.
right.expected_observation: Unary summaries report spurious inequivalence, while relational tests certify equivalence.
right.novelty_reason: This distinguishes representation-preserving behavior from summary-preserving behavior; local semantics does not force the unary-summary failure mode.

right.intervention: Constrain the benchmark to command pairs matched on unary outcomes and then compute relational preimages.
right.expected_observation: At least one matched unary pair separates once outcome-sensitive backward transport is applied.
right.novelty_reason: The shared mother structure predicts a measurable aliasing failure, not just a generic need for richer semantics.

payload.mother_structure: Guarded relation lattice with backward transport

left_fingerprint.constraint_class: Boundary-conditioned skill acquisition over a composable partial action system. Prior authoritative completion evidence labels intervention-bearing edges; current task-open receipts refute reached candidates. A held-out-certified target may be a relation among source factors, operation, and attempted effect, while the runtime currently stores only unary state predicates.
left_fingerprint.abstract_form: Infer a falsifiable task specification over composable partial morphisms and transport it across observation charts without granting prediction task authority.

invariants.carrier: composable partial action relation with guarded operation words
invariants.target: evidence-owned predicate on source-operation-effect morphisms, unary state predicates only a special case
invariants.evidence: authoritative boundary edges provide positives and task-open reached edges provide local refutations
invariants.coordinate_change: joint equivariance may preserve a relation while separately canonicalized factors lose it
invariants.composition: a terminal edge predicate must pull backward through a guarded operation word to an initiation condition
invariants.failure: unary state equality aliases operations or relative orientations with different task consequences

right_fingerprint.constraint_class: Guarded-command and relational program semantics. A command denotes a relation between initial states, operations, and outcomes; a postcondition is transported backward through sequential composition by weakest precondition. Tests witness or refute contracts, while representation changes are valid only when relational behavior commutes.
right_fingerprint.abstract_form: Represent desired behavior as a relational contract and compute the exact precondition of a composed command without identifying the contract with any one coordinate presentation.

invariants.carrier: commands as composable state-transition relations
invariants.target: postcondition or Hoare-style relation over initial state, command, and outcome
invariants.evidence: passing and failing executions constrain candidate contracts but do not manufacture correctness authority
invariants.coordinate_change: simulation or conjugacy preserves relational behavior under representation change
invariants.composition: weakest-precondition or relational preimage composes backward through command sequence
invariants.failure: unary invariants cannot express action-dependent contracts and overidentify behavior

left.prediction: There exists a minimal non-unary held-out target whose backward transport through one guarded operation word is not determined by the learned unary state predicate alone.
left.measurement: Compare prediction error of a unary-only classifier against a triple-relational classifier on a fixed held-out set of source-operation-effect queries.
left.intervention: Collapse the runtime representation to unary predicates, then re-expand by adding one operation-sensitive relational feature and re-evaluate held-out targets.
left.horizon: Within 3 evaluation rounds on the same benchmark split.
left.expected_observation: Unary-only accuracy plateaus while the relation-aware model recovers a previously misclassified family of boundary-conditioned targets.
left.novelty_reason: Local skill-acquisition theory may already motivate action sensitivity, but it does not force the existence of a specific held-out family that becomes separable only after adding one relational lift.

left.prediction: A chart change that preserves the underlying triple relation will preserve cross-chart success even when the individually canonicalized source and effect factors disagree.
left.measurement: Track agreement between charts on the same held-out targets before and after a joint reparameterization.
left.intervention: Apply a nontrivial observation-chart change that jointly mixes source and effect coordinates while keeping the relation fixed.
left.horizon: Across 1 chart transformation and 1 retraining pass.
left.expected_observation: Factorwise features change, but relation-level predictions remain stable for the same held-out targets.
left.novelty_reason: This separates preserved relational behavior from preserved marginals; the side theory alone does not require a chart-mixing invariance test.

left.prediction: A boundary-positive edge and a task-open refutation can coexist on different representatives of the same unary state, forcing a quotient failure visible as a contradiction after backward transport.
left.measurement: Count unary states that map to both positive and refuting edge labels under the same transport rule.
left.intervention: Force two representatives to share the same unary state encoding while keeping their operation words distinct.
left.expected_observation: At least one unary collision produces opposite transport outcomes for distinct operation words.
left.novelty_reason: The mother structure predicts an explicit quotient-collapse witness; neither local theory alone forces this exact collision pattern.

right.prediction: There exists a contract family whose weakest precondition cannot be represented by any unary state invariant without losing outcome sensitivity, but becomes exact after one relational lift.
right.measurement: Compare exactness of inferred preconditions under unary vs relational contract languages on the same command suite.
right.intervention: Replace unary test assertions with relation-aware postconditions while keeping the command sequence fixed.
right.expected_observation: Unary contracts either overapproximate or underapproximate, while relational contracts recover an exact preimage for the same command composition.
right.novelty_reason: Program semantics already admits weakest preconditions, but this prediction isolates a specific lift gap that should appear only when action dependence matters.

right.prediction: A simulation or conjugacy that preserves behavior globally will still fail if tests are projected to unary state summaries, yielding a false mismatch that disappears under relational comparison.
right.measurement: Measure disagreement between unary-summary test results and relation-level equivalence checks under a representation change.
right.intervention: Apply a semantics-preserving reparameterization and evaluate both unary and relational test suites.
right.horizon: Across 1 representation change and 1 regression run.
right.expected_observation: Unary summaries report spurious inequivalence, while relational tests certify equivalence.
right.novelty_reason: This distinguishes representation-preserving behavior from summary-preserving behavior; local semantics does not force the unary-summary failure mode.

right.prediction: Two command sequences with the same unary postcondition will diverge under a relational preimage computed against an outcome-sensitive test, exposing hidden action dependence.
right.measurement: Search for command pairs with identical unary summaries but different weakest preconditions for the same postcondition.
right.intervention: Constrain the benchmark to command pairs matched on unary outcomes and then compute relational preimages.
right.expected_observation: At least one matched unary pair separates once outcome-sensitive backward transport is applied.
right.novelty_reason: The shared mother structure predicts a measurable aliasing failure, not just a generic need for richer semantics.

left_constraint_class: A learned interactive carrier exposes a compressed state quotient q. A relation-valued task accepts source-operation pairs. Runtime found states x,y with q(x)=q(y), the same task-relation truth vector and clock, but q(T_action0(x)) differs from q(T_action0(y)); the erased distinction is completion of a coupled auxiliary marker read by a carrier guard. Decide the invariant-owning representation and safe refinement rule without substrate vocabulary.
right_constraint_class: In deterministic automata, probabilistic bisimulation, and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement, a proposed state partition is invalid when equivalent states have different labeled successor blocks or a distinguishing suffix. The refinement splits only the invalid equivalence class, while acceptance remains a separate observation.
mother_structure: Guarded quotient refinement under witness-preserving observations

left.state: state plus erased coupled auxiliary marker
left.task: relation-valued task truth vector over source-operation pairs
left.failure: same q and same task truth/clock, but different labeled successor quotient because a hidden coordinator marker was omitted
left.authority: external adjudicator over which marker counts

right.failure: equivalent states have different labeled successor blocks or a distinguishing suffix
right.authority: acceptance oracle external to the refinement partition

left.prediction: The correct refinement criterion is not full state splitting but marker-conditioned splitting only on those classes where the same task truth vector appears under the same clock.
left.measurement: Number of classes split by marker-conditioned versus full-state refinement, and preservation of task truth vectors.
left.intervention: Run two refinements: full-state and marker-conditioned, then compare successor consistency and task-vector preservation.
left.expected_observation: Marker-conditioned refinement fixes the counterexample with fewer splits than full-state refinement.
left.novelty_reason: This is a specific minimality claim about the refinement geometry, not implied by local failure alone.

left.prediction: The hidden marker will be detectable by a cross-run instability test: repeating the same source-operation pair after a benign clock-preserving delay will preserve task truth but alter successor quotient only when the marker is present.
left.measurement: Repeated traces over the same pair with a controlled delay and the same clock value.
left.intervention: Insert a bounded benign delay without changing source or task input.
left.expected_observation: Task truth remains fixed while successor quotient divergence appears only in marker-bearing cases.
left.novelty_reason: This predicts a latent temporal detector that local theory of q-equality does not force.

right.prediction: The smallest invalid block will be refuted by a suffix that is also acceptance-neutral, meaning the witness separates transitions without altering acceptance observations.
right.measurement: Acceptance label of the witness path endpoints and the block split outcome.
right.intervention: Search for a shortest distinguishing suffix and record acceptance along the witness.
right.expected_observation: A distinguishing suffix exists whose acceptance observation is unchanged across the compared states.
right.novelty_reason: It constrains the witness to be transition-only, sharpening ordinary counterexample existence.

right.prediction: A refinement that splits only the invalid equivalence class will not cascade into unrelated blocks if the shared mother structure is correct.
right.measurement: Number of downstream block changes outside the invalid class.
right.intervention: Apply the minimal split to the suspect class and re-run partition propagation.
right.expected_observation: Only the invalid class and its direct successors change; unrelated blocks remain fixed.
right.novelty_reason: This tests locality of the mother structure, not just correctness of the split.

left.refuter: A correct fix requires changing terminal relation behavior, not just splitting by the erased marker.
left.gate: Compare pre/post refinement terminal relation-vector audits on a holdout set.
left.receipt: Holdout audit showing a necessary terminal relation change.

left.refuter: The same q-successor mismatch appears even after marker-conditioned splitting.
left.gate: Repeat the original counterexample after minimal marker-aware refinement.
left.receipt: Trace of the repeated mismatch after refinement.

right.refuter: Every shortest distinguishing suffix changes acceptance, so transition-only witnesses do not exist.
right.gate: Shortest suffix search with acceptance tracking.
right.receipt: Witness log with acceptance deltas along all minimal separators.

right.refuter: Minimal splitting necessarily cascades into unrelated blocks.
right.gate: Partition propagation trace after one local split.
right.receipt: Block-diff report showing unrelated changes.

left.authority: external adjudicator that certifies which distinctions count

right.task: acceptance kept separate from transition partition
right.failure: equivalent states admit a distinguishing successor block or suffix
right.authority: external acceptance oracle separate from partition refinement

left.prediction: If the carrier guard is the true invariant owner, then there exists a smallest refinement that restores successor consistency without changing any terminal relation-vector values for already-separated classes.
left.measurement: Count of equivalence classes before and after refinement, plus a holdout test on terminal relation-vector agreement over a fixed validation set of source-operation pairs.
left.intervention: Introduce a candidate refinement keyed only by the suspected erased marker, then rerun the same action on matched q-classes.
left.horizon: Within 1 refinement round and 1 validation replay.
left.expected_observation: Exactly the previously failing q-equal pair splits, while all terminal relation-vector values on unaffected classes remain unchanged.
left.novelty_reason: Local theory of the observed quotient only says the current partition fails; it does not force a minimal marker-only split with unchanged terminal relation statistics.

left.prediction: A second action label that bypasses the suspected marker will fail to reproduce the discrepancy, even when applied to the same q-equal pair.
left.measurement: Difference in q(T_action(x)) versus q(T_action(y)) across a small action-labeled test suite.
left.intervention: Swap the action label to a guard-bypassing variant while holding source states fixed.
left.expected_observation: The mismatch disappears for at least one bypass action but persists for the original action.
left.novelty_reason: This predicts label-sensitive failure localization, not just generic non-congruence.

right.prediction: The invalid block should admit a one-step splitter whose witness is a single distinguishing successor class rather than a long counterexample suffix.
right.measurement: Length of the shortest counterexample suffix and number of blocks created by the refinement procedure.
right.intervention: Run one partition-refinement pass with the current suspect block forced to split on immediate labeled successors.
right.expected_observation: A one-step successor witness suffices to separate the block; no deeper suffix is needed for this invalid class.
right.novelty_reason: Standard invalidity permits arbitrary distinguishing suffixes; this predicts a strictly local witness shape.

right.prediction: Acceptance observations remain invariant under the minimal split that repairs successor congruence.
right.measurement: Acceptance label on each refined block before and after splitting.
right.intervention: Apply the minimal splitter and recompute acceptance annotations.
right.expected_observation: At least one block splits, but acceptance labels of all descendants match the parent acceptance observation.
right.novelty_reason: This is a stronger separation between transition refinement and acceptance than generic bisimulation failure requires.

left_constraint_class: An interactive ARC controller persists symbolic episode logs, compressed skills, and decision receipts, but the model reasoning process is absent from action selection and any LLM calls are fresh single-message Chat Completions. Nonterminal discoveries therefore survive only if a hand-built projection has already encoded them.

right_forbidden_domain: neural substrate vocabulary and biological implementation details
mother_structure: Conjectural action-path bundle with holonomy compression

left.actor: Policy map on observable base states, instantiated by the deterministic planner
left.fast_state: Path-fiber coordinate forced to the identity at every decision boundary
left.slow_state: Archive of manually compressed path and cycle summaries
left.update_locus: Hand-specified projection from paths into archive coordinates
left.credit_horizon: Prefix valuation is zero unless the projection explicitly preserves it
left.equality: Equality of base state, controller, context key, and admissible-action fiber
left.intervention_cost: Edge cost assigned to each primitive action

right.actor: Policy map jointly reading the observable base state and current path-fiber coordinate
right.fast_state: Nontrivial fiber coordinate transported across successive action-observation edges
right.slow_state: Archive of selected path and cycle summaries
right.update_locus: Online fiber transport followed by slower projection into the archive
right.credit_horizon: Prefix valuations transported across multiple edges
right.equality: Equality of base state, context key, and admissible-action fiber
right.intervention_cost: Edge cost assigned to action and selective-observation choices

left.prediction: For endpoint-matched path pairs that produce byte-identical existing archive records, one signed cycle coordinate will improve later decisions selectively when the two action transports are order-sensitive.
left.measurement: Terminal completion-rate difference between the augmented and baseline controllers, stratified by preregistered order-sensitive and order-insensitive path pairs with identical task, controller, endpoint context, and feasible choices
left.intervention: Extend the compiler with one signed coordinate distinguishing AB from BA; compare against equal-byte random-coordinate and path-length controls
left.horizon: 240 held-out episodes of at most 12 actions, spanning two archive-revision cycles
left.expected_observation: At least a 12-percentage-point gain on order-sensitive pairs, no more than a 3-point gain on order-insensitive pairs, and no more than a 3-point gain from either control
left.novelty_reason: A reset-plus-archive account does not select action commutators as the missing statistic. The selective interaction follows from the conjectured path-composition law.

right.prediction: Endpoint-conditioned retrieval will respect path equivalence under insertion of an action followed by its learned inverse, while a same-length noninverse insertion will disrupt retrieval.
right.measurement: Accuracy and choice-probability shift at an observably identical endpoint after trained AB and BA paths, comparing bare, inverse-pair, and noninverse-pair probes
right.intervention: Train distinct endpoint choices for AB and BA paths, then insert either CC-inverse or CD before the endpoint while holding path length, endpoint, and outcome schedule fixed
right.horizon: Immediate test and one delayed test within 48 hours
right.expected_observation: Endpoint-conditioned accuracy above 65%; less than a 5-point change after inverse-pair insertion; at least a 12-point decrease after matched noninverse insertion
right.novelty_reason: Persistent task state permits order effects but does not require inverse-pair invariance. That algebraic equivalence is imposed by the conjectured mother structure.

left.prediction: For endpoint-matched path pairs that produce byte-identical existing archive records, one signed cycle coordinate will improve later decisions selectively when the two action transports are order-sensitive.
left.measurement: Terminal completion-rate difference between the augmented and baseline controllers, stratified by preregistered order-sensitive and order-insensitive path pairs with identical task, controller, endpoint context, and feasible choices
left.intervention: Extend the compiler with one signed coordinate distinguishing AB from BA; compare against equal-byte random-coordinate and path-length controls
left.horizon: 240 held-out episodes of at most 12 actions, spanning two archive-revision cycles
left.expected_observation: At least a 12-percentage-point gain on order-sensitive pairs, no more than a 3-point gain on order-insensitive pairs, and no more than a 3-point gain from either control
left.novelty_reason: A reset-plus-archive account does not select action commutators as the missing statistic. The selective interaction follows from the conjectured path-composition law.

right.prediction: Endpoint-conditioned retrieval will respect path equivalence under insertion of an action followed by its learned inverse, while a same-length noninverse insertion will disrupt retrieval.
right.measurement: Accuracy and choice-probability shift at an observably identical endpoint after trained AB and BA paths, comparing bare, inverse-pair, and noninverse-pair probes
right.intervention: Train distinct endpoint choices for AB and BA paths, then insert either CC-inverse or CD before the endpoint while holding path length, endpoint, and outcome schedule fixed
right.horizon: Immediate test and one delayed test within 48 hours
right.expected_observation: Endpoint-conditioned accuracy above 65%; less than a 5-point change after inverse-pair insertion; at least a 12-point decrease after matched noninverse insertion
right.novelty_reason: Persistent task state permits order effects but does not require inverse-pair invariance. That algebraic equivalence is imposed by the conjectured mother structure.

left.prediction: Next-sleep replay priority will track a retrieved schema's causal marginal contribution to a compatible outcome, rather than raw reward, surprise, retrieval frequency, or recency.
left.measurement: Per-schema change in decoded sequential-reactivation probability from night 1 to night 2, combined with the randomized retrieval-prompt effect on decision accuracy.
left.intervention: Randomly prompt or sham-prompt schema retrieval immediately before decisions; cross this with guard-compatible versus guard-violating contexts and matched positive or negative feedback.
left.expected_observation: Replay increases after retrievals that causally improve compatible decisions, decreases after retrievals that causally impair them, and remains unchanged when identical outcomes follow sham retrieval or guard-violating use.
left.novelty_reason: Outcome-modulated replay alone leaves marginal attribution and compatibility unspecified; the predicted retrieval-by-compatibility interaction is an additional discriminator.

left.prediction: A first compatible contradiction will produce a transient rebound in replay of the schema's exact source episodes; repeated matching contradictions will subsequently suppress schema replay.
left.measurement: Source-episode reactivation, schema-level replay, and context-specific transfer measured after each contradiction and sleep period.
left.intervention: Deliver either one or three matched-surprise contradictions inside the learned schema guard, with an equally surprising outside-guard contradiction as control.
left.expected_observation: One inside-guard contradiction selectively raises source-episode replay during the next sleep; repeated inside-guard contradictions then lower schema replay, while outside-guard contradictions produce neither transition.
left.novelty_reason: Reconsolidation and downscaling permit several temporal orderings; a compatibility-gated reopen-then-retire sequence is a narrower, falsifiable commitment.

right.prediction: Future skill-recall weight will track randomized retrieval's marginal contribution to compatible externally judged outcomes while primitive action cost remains invariant.

right.intervention: Randomly inject or withhold each eligible skill on guard-compatible and guard-incompatible episodes while keeping the controller, primitive prices, and external authority fixed.
right.horizon: Four hundred decisions and two compiler cycles.
right.expected_observation: Recall weight changes with the signed inject-versus-ablate effect only on compatible episodes; raw use count loses predictive power after that effect is included, and primitive-cost distributions remain within 2% of control.
right.novelty_reason: Missing outcome-linked credit can be repaired in many ways; counterfactual settlement, guard interaction, and cost separation are additional commitments.

prediction_cards.horizon: Four hundred decisions and two compiler cycles.
prediction_cards.expected_observation: Recall weight changes with the signed inject-versus-ablate effect only on compatible episodes; raw use count loses predictive power after that effect is included, and primitive-cost distributions remain within 2% of control.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Missing outcome-linked credit can be repaired in many ways; counterfactual settlement, guard interaction, and cost separation are additional commitments.
prediction_cards.refuter: Recall updates follow use count or total reward while randomized marginal contribution and compatibility add no predictive value.
prediction_cards.gate: Kill if marginal-contribution rank correlation with later recall is at most 0.10 across five seeds while use-count correlation is at least 0.30, or if primitive costs shift by more than 2%.
prediction_cards.receipt: Immutable inject-ablate assignments, outcome receipts, recall-weight history, cost traces, and seed-level correlations.

prediction_cards.prediction: One compatible authoritative failure will temporarily increase replay of a skill's linked receipts before repeated matching failures demote the compiled skill.
prediction_cards.measurement: Receipt identifiers entering the compiler queue, skill-retrieval weight by cycle, recompilation events, and primitive action costs.
prediction_cards.intervention: Inject one versus three authoritative rejections for matched inputs inside a skill guard, alongside equally severe rejections outside that guard.
prediction_cards.horizon: Three compiler cycles or 150 subsequent episodes.
prediction_cards.expected_observation: The first inside-guard rejection raises linked-receipt replay without immediately erasing the skill; repeated rejections lower retrieval weight. Outside-guard rejections leave both quantities unchanged.
prediction_cards.novelty_reason: Direct demotion and permanent retention are both compatible with the local design; the proposed probationary reopening state is independently testable.
prediction_cards.refuter: Receipt reopening is absent, guard-insensitive, or never followed by demotion under repeated failure.
prediction_cards.gate: Kill if the predicted reopen-then-demote ordering appears in fewer than four of five deterministic seeds.
prediction_cards.receipt: Compiler queue snapshots, provenance links, authority verdicts, skill-state transitions, and replay-order logs.

left_constraint_class: One intervention response is externally identified at one typed local state. Reuse at a changed state is unsafe because only a partial correspondence is observed, false transfer has cost, and scalar value erases which transition was changed. Two-hop reuse must expose path inconsistency rather than average it away.
right_constraint_class: A sparse partial cue reactivates a distributed local assembly. A transient local tag marks recently changed connections; a delayed global modulator changes only tagged connections. Reactivation under a changed sensory chart remains useful only when downstream prediction error agrees, while replay around inconsistent routes should suppress or split the assembly.

left.false_transfer_cost: cost of moving the wrong operator across states
left.loop_defect: boolean detector of nontrivial transport cycle

right.eligibility_tag: tag relation on recently changed transitions
right.cycle_inconsistency: boolean detector of inconsistent replay cycle

left.prediction: Operator transport will be robust only when a defect-aware composition rule is used; naive averaging over two-hop paths will hide a failure mode that appears as a false-transfer spike on one branch.
left.measurement: Branchwise transfer cost versus path-averaged transfer cost.
left.intervention: Compare averaged versus branch-resolved transport in a deliberately inconsistent loop.
left.expected_observation: Averaging masks the defect while branchwise accounting reveals it.
left.novelty_reason: This predicts a measurable mismatch between aggregated and path-resolved analysis.

left.prediction: Changing the typed local state while keeping the same operator identity will preserve delayed value only when the operator transport relation carries a compatible loop-defect parity.
left.measurement: Delayed-value preservation conditioned on loop-defect parity.
left.intervention: Flip the path parity without changing the transported operator class.
left.expected_observation: Parity-preserving routes keep value stable; parity-flipping routes do not.
left.novelty_reason: This is a parity-conditioned transport law, not a generic state transition law.

right.prediction: Reactivation through a chart change will be accepted when the transported local dynamics retain the same downstream-error parity, but inconsistent replay cycles will force a split even if the cue identity is unchanged.
right.measurement: Acceptance rate and split rate as a function of downstream-error parity.
right.intervention: Engineer replay routes with matched cue identity but different parity of transported prediction error.
right.expected_observation: Parity-matched routes remain unified; parity-mismatched routes split.
right.novelty_reason: The prediction introduces an error-parity gate on replay consistency.

right.prediction: Eligibility tags will behave as a transport filter: delayed modulation will change only those transitions whose chart-change history is compatible with the same sparse-address class.
right.measurement: Selective change rate on transitions grouped by sparse-address compatibility.
right.intervention: Perturb chart-change history while holding the sparse-address cue fixed.
right.horizon: Immediately after the delayed modulator arrives.
right.expected_observation: Only compatible transitions update strongly.
right.novelty_reason: This adds a history-compatibility filter beyond simple tagging.

left_fingerprint.constraint_class: One intervention response is externally identified at one typed local state. Reuse at a changed state is unsafe because only a partial correspondence is observed, false transfer has cost, and scalar value erases which transition was changed. left_fingerprint.abstract_form: Given a family of local fibers with partial maps, transport a valued endomorphism from one fiber to another only when the mapped endomorphism square commutes and a delayed consequence functional is preserved; compose transports while detecting nontrivial loop defect.

right_fingerprint.constraint_class: A sparse partial cue reactivates a distributed local assembly. A transient local tag marks recently changed connections; a delayed global modulator changes only tagged connections. Reactivation under a changed sensory chart remains useful only when downstream prediction error agrees, while replay around inconsistent routes should suppress or split the assembly.
right_fingerprint.abstract_form: A sparsely addressed local subspace carries temporary eligibility marks; a delayed global functional updates marked transitions; chart-changing reactivation is accepted only when transported local dynamics predict the same downstream functional, and inconsistent cycles induce separation.

left.prediction: If the same transported endomorphism is applied through two different admissible local paths with equal target-state typing, then the discrepancy will concentrate in a cycle defect term rather than in the delayed-value term.
left.measurement: Difference between delayed-value outcomes under two-hop transports, plus an independently computed loop-defect indicator on the path pair.
left.intervention: Construct matched path pairs that differ only by a single intermediate state change and compare transported endomorphisms.
left.horizon: Within two transport steps after the first intervention.
left.expected_observation: One path pair preserves delayed value while the other exhibits a nonzero loop defect and a localized transfer penalty.
left.novelty_reason: Local transport theory alone can accept each path separately; this predicts a path-comparison signature only visible when two transports are juxtaposed.

left.prediction: A transport rule that preserves delayed value on one fiber will fail to generalize to a second fiber unless the partial correspondence relation composes associatively on the shared overlap.
left.measurement: Success/failure of value preservation under repeated reuse across three fibers with a controlled overlap pattern.
left.intervention: Force reuse of the same intervention operator on a third fiber after altering the intermediate correspondence map.
left.expected_observation: Value preservation breaks exactly when overlap composition changes, even if each single-step map remains admissible.
left.novelty_reason: This isolates a higher-order reuse constraint not forced by single-hop admissibility.

left.prediction: False-transfer cost will be minimized by a path-selection rule that explicitly scores loop defect, not by any rule that only optimizes local correspondence quality.
left.measurement: Empirical comparison of transfer cost under path selection by local fit versus path selection by defect-penalized fit.
left.intervention: Deploy two selection heuristics over the same candidate transports: one local-only, one defect-aware.
left.horizon: Over a short batch of transports on the same fiber family.
left.expected_observation: Defect-aware selection yields lower aggregate false-transfer cost on cases with nontrivial loop structure.
left.novelty_reason: A local theory of single transitions does not force a global defect-aware selector.

right.prediction: A replayed assembly will split into two downstream patterns when chart-changing reactivation preserves sparse address but reverses the order of two inconsistent routes.
right.measurement: Count and identity of downstream assemblies after replay under route order reversal.
right.intervention: Replay the same cue through two route orderings while holding the eligible tag set fixed.
right.horizon: Within the first replay cycle after the cue.
right.expected_observation: One route ordering maintains a single assembly; the other produces a separated pair with distinct downstream-error signatures.
right.novelty_reason: This is a path-order effect, not a simple cue-response effect.

right.prediction: If the delayed global modulator is delivered before the chart change rather than after it, downstream error will rise selectively on tagged transitions and the assembly will not remain stable.
right.measurement: Downstream error magnitude and assembly stability after swapped timing of modulation and chart change.
right.intervention: Swap the order of modulation and chart remapping while keeping the tag pattern fixed.
right.expected_observation: Premature modulation yields higher error and weaker assembly coherence than delayed modulation.
right.novelty_reason: Timing-specific eligibility dependence is not implied by a static cue-assembly model.

right.prediction: When two reactivation routes are downstream-equivalent but differ in chart transport, the system will accept the route with lower transported prediction error and suppress the inconsistent one rather than averaging them.
right.measurement: Acceptance probability, suppression rate, and downstream-error comparison across route pairs.
right.intervention: Present two chart-distinct routes to the same local subspace and manipulate their transported dynamics to be error-matched or error-mismatched.
right.horizon: Across a small replay set within one session.
right.expected_observation: Error-matched routes are jointly accepted; error-mismatched routes are separated or one is suppressed.
right.novelty_reason: This predicts a transport-level gate, not just cue recognition.

left_constraint_class: An agent makes chains of nonterminal protocol decisions in an unfamiliar interactive task. Externally settled outcomes arrive later. Content-addressed skills or advice can be offered or withheld at one exact recurrent controller parent. Credit must attach only to content that changes later object-linked proposals and downstream outcome, while exact authority coordinates and primitive costs are preserved. Repeated matched evidence may consolidate a reusable response.
right_constraint_class: During sparse-reward biological learning, recurrent cortical and hippocampal assemblies active across a behavior sequence leave transient synaptic eligibility marks. Delayed neuromodulatory consequences modify selected marked transitions; replay or reactivation consolidates useful chunks, while circuit and context gating limits maladaptive transfer. The system must distinguish causal memory content from generic activation.

left.prediction: Credit should depend on the interaction between intervention identity and exact fork identity, so the same content can earn opposite eligibility at two observationally similar parents.
left.measurement: For each content hash, estimate the matched offer-minus-withhold outcome difference separately at two parents sharing visible task features but having different typed histories.
left.intervention: Randomize offer versus withhold independently at each parent while holding resumed state action prices and downstream evaluator fixed.
left.horizon: At least 40 matched pairs per parent or 14 days, whichever occurs first.
left.expected_observation: The parent-by-content interaction exceeds the pooled content effect, with at least one content hash showing opposite-signed effects whose 90% intervals exclude zero.
left.novelty_reason: The local eligibility rule requires exact authority coordinates but does not by itself predict sign reversal between superficially equivalent parents.

left.prediction: A delayed settlement should cease to confer credit once the charged path crosses a typed namespace boundary, even if temporal distance and outcome value are unchanged.
left.measurement: Compare credited byte-level content contributions for equal-delay paths that either remain within one namespace or cross exactly one registered scope boundary.
left.intervention: Insert a semantics-preserving action-vocabulary identity change halfway through randomly selected resumed chains.
left.expected_observation: Within-scope chains retain a positive matched credit estimate, whereas boundary-crossing chains fall to within 10% of the offer-withhold null unless an explicit compatibility morphism is supplied.
left.novelty_reason: Pricing and delayed credit alone do not force a sharp boundary effect or its rescue by an explicit compatibility witness.

right.horizon: One delayed consequence plus three replay episodes within 24 hours.
right.expected_observation: Tag-conditioned efficacy and choice effects reverse sign across histories, while untagged neighboring transitions remain within 10% of baseline drift.
right.novelty_reason: Generic selective-update accounts do not force historical identity to reverse the sign under matched current activity.

right.novelty_reason: Context gating alone does not force a morphism-like bridge rescue with transition-level selectivity.

left_constraint_class: An agent makes chains of nonterminal protocol decisions in an unfamiliar interactive task. Externally settled outcomes arrive later. Content-addressed skills or advice can be offered or withheld at one exact recurrent controller parent. Credit must attach only to content that changes later object-linked proposals and downstream outcome, while exact authority coordinates and primitive costs are preserved. Repeated matched evidence may consolidate a reusable response.
right_constraint_class: During sparse-reward biological learning, recurrent cortical and hippocampal assemblies active across a behavior sequence leave transient synaptic eligibility marks. Delayed neuromodulatory consequences modify selected marked transitions; replay or reactivation consolidates useful chunks, while circuit and context gating limits maladaptive transfer. The system must distinguish causal memory content from generic activation.

left.measurement: Estimate matched causal credit across a factorial grid of intervention bytes and charged-chain lengths while controlling content identity and primitive cost.

left.prediction: Consolidation should preserve outcome-relevant proposal differences but discard intervention details that never alter descendant proposals, producing a measurable minimum sufficient macro.
left.measurement: Compare macro description length replay fidelity descendant-proposal divergence and settled outcome across progressive content ablations.

left.expected_observation: A sharp ablation point appears: deleting below it reduces bytes without changing proposals, while deleting the next component increases proposal divergence by at least 20% and erases at least half the outcome advantage.

right.expected_observation: Selective modification collapses along a common complexity-delay frontier; equal-complexity reductions extend the effective delay window without increasing untargeted change.
right.novelty_reason: Finite trace lifetime alone predicts temporal decay but not a tradeoff between representational complexity and admissible delay.

right.novelty_reason: Replay-associated consolidation does not alone force an information-ranked minimum subset or a sharp boundary.

left_fingerprint.constraint_class: An agent makes chains of nonterminal protocol decisions in an unfamiliar interactive task. Externally settled outcomes arrive later. Content-addressed skills or advice can be offered or withheld at one exact recurrent controller parent. Credit must attach only to content that changes later object-linked proposals and downstream outcome, while exact authority coordinates and primitive costs are preserved. Repeated matched evidence may consolidate a reusable response.

left_constraint_class: A controller emits successive protocol-choice windows during an ARC run. Each window has exact task, source context, continuation controller, full choice set, selected option, and primitive cost. Terminal external adjudication arrives later. Exact counterfactual arms require a replay contract; unrelated runs must never be paired. Predicted information yield exists at selection time but observed information yield needs a compatible later receipt.
right_constraint_class: Brains bind hippocampal episodes, maintain finite synaptic eligibility traces, apply delayed neuromodulatory reward-prediction errors, replay experiences offline, and train basal-ganglia action selection. Similar episodes are not automatically identical counterfactuals, and novelty signals remain distinct from reward.

left.authority: controller_state = exact task/source_context/continuation_controller/choice_set
left.delay: eligibility_trace = finite window lifetime before external adjudication
left.cost: primitive_cost = intervention effort paid at choice time, invariant under later value
left.pairing: replay_contract = sealed provenance link between choice window and later receipt
left.signals: predicted_information_yield = selection-time surprise estimate, observed_information_yield = receipt-time compatible surprise

right.authority: episode_state = hippocampal episode/context/action_set identity
right.delay: synaptic_trace = finite eligibility lifetime before neuromodulatory outcome
right.cost: action_effort = execution cost separated from learned value
right.signals: novelty_signal = pre-outcome surprise distinct from reward_prediction_error

left.measurement: Count receipt-eligible pairings produced by replay checker under a controlled context-swap while holding task and choice-set fixed.
left.intervention: Create matched ARC windows with identical task/source/choice-set but different continuation controllers and issue the same delayed receipt distribution.
left.horizon: Within one ARC run and its immediate delayed receipt batch.
left.expected_observation: Pairing success rate should drop to near zero for swapped-controller windows even when local reward is identical.
left.novelty_reason: Local ARC choice logic can accept reward-equivalent windows; it does not force a controller-identity test on delayed credit binding.

left_constraint_class: A credited episode nominates a source operation word that the current carrier can lower into generative search, but no persistent object chooses cross-task abstractions or earns credit from a later non-equivalent acquisition.
right_constraint_class: Episodic experiences are replayed into persistent relational schemas that later contexts instantiate through local motor systems; reward and prediction error determine which schema persists and how quickly a different competence is learned.
left_forbidden_domain: interactive skill acquisition, hierarchical reinforcement learning, and program-library learning
right_forbidden_domain: systems neuroscience, hippocampal replay, cortical schema consolidation, and motor learning

left.carrier: A state-indexed realization functor required to predict every primitive image before transfer
left.episode: A provenance-bearing nomination record with no execution authority
left.authority: A non-transferable settlement token issued by an external boundary
left.source_program: An abstract operation word awaiting realization through the source-indexed functor
left.target_program: A target-indexed realization expressed solely in the target namespace
left.lowering: A prospective commutation certificate, or typed refusal, between abstract and target-local execution
left.estimand: The difference in child-acquisition cost with versus without access to settled parent schemas
left.cost: Total contact, deliberation, construction, retrieval, verification, execution, and error expenditure
left.update: A measured cost derivative that updates schema selection and realization-proposal probabilities
left.failure: Localized posterior demotion of the failed schema-to-target edge

right.episode: A provenance-bearing nomination record encoded by an ordered event trace
right.replay: Generation of candidate abstract relation words from nomination records
right.schema: A persistent abstract relation carrying learned settlement weight
right.instantiation: A context-indexed realization functor into local sensorimotor coordinates
right.reward: A delayed settlement signal that changes schema weight without transmitting local commands
right.prediction_error: A commutation residual between schema-predicted and observed local transitions
right.transfer: Reduced acquisition cost for a non-equivalent realization of the same candidate schema
right.cost: Total experience and deliberation expenditure before criterion performance
right.selection: Competition among schemas and schema-to-context edges under bounded persistence capacity
right.failure: Typed refusal or localized reconsolidation of the implicated schema-to-context edge

left.prediction: A parent abstraction will reduce target acquisition cost only when a prospective commutation certificate is produced before the first target outcome; equally credited parents lacking that certificate will not help.
left.measurement: Matched difference in total acquisition cost and trials-to-criterion across certificate-present, certificate-absent, and parent-library-absent conditions
left.intervention: Randomly expose eligible target learners to a valid prospective certificate, a structurally plausible certificate with one deliberately broken primitive image, or no parent schema
left.horizon: The first 20 target contacts or 4 hours of target work, whichever occurs first
left.expected_observation: Valid certificates lower median acquisition cost; broken certificates trigger refusal or localized edge demotion rather than broad library suppression; uncertified access is indistinguishable from absence
left.novelty_reason: The left-side formulation requires prospective lowering but does not by itself force the interaction between certificate validity, settlement credit, and localized persistence.

left.prediction: Delayed external credit assigned to a parent after target work has begun will alter future reuse probability but will not retroactively improve the already-observed target trajectory.
left.measurement: Change in proposal probability for the credited abstraction on the next three non-equivalent tasks, alongside pre-credit versus post-credit target cost
left.intervention: Randomize whether an identical parent settlement token is revealed before target contact, midway through acquisition, or only after criterion
left.horizon: Current target episode plus the next three eligible tasks
left.expected_observation: Midway or late credit changes later abstraction selection without discontinuously improving completed target actions; early credit helps only when coupled to a valid target certificate
left.novelty_reason: This temporal dissociation follows from the shared separation of nomination, settlement, and realization, rather than from ordinary library reuse.

right.prediction: Replay should predict later transfer only when it contains a prospective relation-to-context compatibility signal; replay count alone should cease predicting savings after compatibility is controlled.
right.measurement: Trial-level replay count, decoded relational content, pre-behavior compatibility score, and experiences-to-criterion on a non-equivalent task
right.intervention: During offline periods, selectively enhance replay events decoded as compatibility-bearing, enhance equally frequent episode-specific replay, or apply sham stimulation
right.horizon: One offline interval followed by no more than 100 adaptation trials
right.expected_observation: Enhancing compatibility-bearing replay reduces adaptation cost; enhancing episode-specific replay without compatibility content does not, despite matched replay frequency
right.novelty_reason: The right-side theory links replay and schemas but does not locally force a prospective commutation-like certificate to dominate replay frequency.

right.prediction: A large prediction error confined to one context realization will reduce reuse of that schema-context pairing while preserving the same schema's transfer benefit in a different compatible context.
right.measurement: Post-error schema decoding, context-specific reinstatement, and trials-to-criterion in the failed context and a second compatible context
right.intervention: Introduce an unannounced context-specific reversal that invalidates local realization while preserving the abstract relation, compared with a reversal that invalidates the relation itself
right.horizon: The reversal block and two transfer probes within 48 hours
right.expected_observation: Local-realization reversal produces context-specific suppression and preserved transfer elsewhere; relation-level reversal produces cross-context schema suppression
right.novelty_reason: This sharp lesion pattern is imported from edge-local credit assignment in the mother structure and is not implied merely by reconsolidation or prediction error.

left.prediction: Persistent abstractions selected by estimated adaptation savings will outperform abstractions selected by historical reuse count when task families have unequal contact costs.
left.measurement: Out-of-sample total acquisition cost, refusal precision, and abstraction-selection frequency on held-out non-equivalent targets
left.intervention: Randomly rank an identical candidate pool by estimated counterfactual savings, episode frequency, or unweighted prior credit
left.horizon: Ten held-out targets or 30 days, whichever occurs first
left.expected_observation: Savings-ranked selection lowers aggregate cost and refuses more incompatible transfers even when it reuses some abstractions less frequently
left.novelty_reason: Neither persistent program reuse nor local cost accounting alone forces a market-like comparison between counterfactual savings and historical popularity.

left.prediction: Artificially subsidizing primitive contact cost will increase attempted lowerings but can decrease net abstraction value by admitting high-deliberation, high-error transfers.
left.measurement: Attempt rate, full cost decomposition, negative-transfer rate, and subsequent abstraction-edge weights
left.intervention: Provide free primitive observations for half of matched targets while holding deliberation, verification, execution, and error costs unchanged
left.horizon: One acquisition episode per target plus the next five proposal decisions
left.expected_observation: Subsidized targets receive more proposals but do not necessarily show lower total cost; losses selectively demote translation edges dominated by hidden downstream costs
left.novelty_reason: The prediction depends on treating all cost components as a clearing price rather than equating cheap contact with transferable usefulness.

right.prediction: Schemas with fewer replay events but larger estimated counterfactual adaptation savings will receive more consolidation resources than frequently replayed low-savings schemas when consolidation capacity is restricted.
right.measurement: Replay count, decoded schema identity, estimated experiences-saved, post-offline retention, and subsequent transfer speed
right.intervention: Train two schemas with crossed replay frequency and adaptation-savings estimates, then restrict the offline consolidation interval
right.horizon: One restricted offline interval and transfer testing within 24 hours
right.expected_observation: Retention and transfer favor the high-savings schema over the high-frequency schema despite fewer replay events
right.novelty_reason: Reward-modulated consolidation does not alone require selection by a counterfactual savings price under a capacity constraint.

right.prediction: Reducing sensory exposure cost while leaving planning demands intact will increase schema instantiation attempts without improving, and sometimes worsening, net adaptation efficiency.
right.measurement: Instantiation attempts, sensory samples, deliberation time, motor errors, reward, and trials-to-criterion
right.intervention: Provide an enriched preview that makes local observations cheap but does not disclose the context-to-action mapping, compared with a matched standard-preview condition
right.horizon: A maximum of 80 trials in a novel non-equivalent context
right.expected_observation: Enriched preview increases early schema commitments; incompatible schemas incur greater deliberation or error costs, so full adaptation cost fails to track sensory exposure cost
right.novelty_reason: This cost-component dissociation is inherited from the mother market and is not forced by standard replay, reward, or motor-error accounts.
